headline: Learned models now predict binding, design and specificity from structure and sequence
label: Machine Learning Protein Prediction
summary: Several new predictors for binding, design and property tasks rely on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure inputs.
synthesis: Items apply learned models to distinct prediction and design problems: PROTAC design with linker-conditioned diffusion (DesignMaster), RNA-small molecule pocket detection with transfer learning (SMARTPocket), antibody CDR sequence-structure co-design from noisy retrieved templates (NT-ABDiff), distogram-guided steering of AlphaFold2 toward alternative conformations (SteerAF), and sequence-only antibody-antigen affinity from frozen ESM-2 embeddings (AbAffinity, Pearson r 0.838). Published work adds residue-level splittable site prediction from sequence and structure (SplitSeek-Pro) and paired-chain TCR binding specificity prediction (TCRBinder, AUC-ROC 0.911, with gains on unseen cases). The dominant thread is conditioning generative or predictive models on auxiliary structural, template, or sequence-derived information, rather than a uniform advance shared by every item. Newer elements include treating noisy templates as reweighted inputs, inference-time steering of a fixed predictor, and chain-aware pairing in language-model embeddings.
